scenes.visual: Title card 'Leak and Push-Back' fades in over a cartoon iron stove with wavy heat lines. THE WORLD, kept for both films (16:9, warm cream background, flat cartoon shapes, no molecular structures). COLOUR MAP, same in every scene and in the second film: INSIDE (the regulated variable) = TEAL bar or level, labelled with the variable's name; OUTSIDE = ORANGE bar or level; LEAK = ORANGE arrow from outside toward inside, its thickness = the actual leak flow, which grows with the gap between outside and inside; PUSH-BACK = TEAL arrow pointing toward the set point, its thickness = the actual push-back flow, which grows with the gap from the set point; whenever the inside has settled, the two arrows are drawn equally thick, at every dial setting. STRENGTHS are dials, never arrows: LEAK STRENGTH = ORANGE dial, PUSH-BACK STRENGTH = TEAL dial; the fraction leak strength ÷ (leak strength + push-back strength) compares the dials. SET POINT = dashed TEAL line. Loop parts always named in this order and these words: regulated variable, set point, sensor, integrator, effector. Anything not computed is labelled 'schematic'.

scenes.tts: In a room hot enough to cook an egg, why didn't the man cook? In 1775, Charles Blagden sat in a room heated close to the boiling point of water. On another visit, eggs in that room roasted hard.
scenes.visual: A cartoon room with an iron stove. A wall thermometer fills with ORANGE to a label 'about 200 °F (about 93 °C)'. A man in 18th-century coat sits in a chair, labelled 'Charles Blagden, 1775'. On a side table an egg sits under a small tag 'separate visit'. A question mark pulses between man and egg.
scenes.narration: In a room hot enough to cook an egg, why didn't the man cook? In 1775, Charles Blagden sat in a room heated close to the boiling point of water. On another visit, eggs in that room roasted hard.

scenes.tts: Start with the egg. Hot air pours heat into it. Nothing pushes back. So the egg keeps warming toward the air's temperature. It cooks along the way.
scenes.visual: Zoom to the egg. Beside it, a tall ORANGE bar labelled 'outside: air' and a short TEAL bar labelled 'inside: egg'. A thick ORANGE arrow labelled 'leak' runs from the orange bar into the egg. The TEAL bar rises steadily toward the ORANGE bar's top. Partway up, well below the air's level, the egg turns opaque white and gains a 'cooked' tag, while the TEAL bar keeps climbing toward the air.
scenes.narration: Start with the egg. Hot air pours heat into it. Nothing pushes back. So the egg keeps warming toward the air's temperature. It cooks along the way.

scenes.tts: Now the man. The same air pours heat into him. Call that flow the leak. Yet the thermometer under his tongue barely moved. It stayed about one degree above his usual.
scenes.visual: Pan to Blagden. Same tall ORANGE outside bar; an ORANGE 'leak' arrow now points into his body. His TEAL bar, labelled 'inside: core temperature', starts low and twitches up by only a hair. A small glass thermometer under his tongue shows '98 °F' on screen; caption 'about 1 degree above his usual'.
scenes.narration: Now the man. The same air pours heat into him. Call that flow the leak. Yet the thermometer under his tongue barely moved. It stayed about one degree above his usual.

scenes.tts: Something in his body pulled the other way. Call it push-back. Leak drags the inside toward the outside. Push-back drags it toward a fixed value.
scenes.visual: A TEAL arrow labelled 'push-back' grows out of the body, pointing down toward a dashed TEAL line drawn across his TEAL bar, labelled 'set point'. The ORANGE leak arrow pushes the bar up; the TEAL push-back arrow pushes it back down; the bar jiggles and holds near the dashed line.
scenes.narration: Something in his body pulled the other way. Call it push-back. Leak drags the inside toward the outside. Push-back drags it toward a fixed value.

scenes.tts: Push-back comes from a loop with five parts. First, the regulated variable, the quantity being held. Here it is core body temperature. Second, the set point, the reference value it is held around.
scenes.visual: The TEAL push-back arrow unfolds into a loop diagram drawn around the TEAL bar, one box at a time. Box 1 lights: 'regulated variable: core temperature' attached to the TEAL bar. Box 2 lights: 'set point', attached to the dashed TEAL line.
scenes.narration: Push-back comes from a loop with five parts. First, the regulated variable, the quantity being held. Here it is core body temperature. Second, the set point, the reference value it is held around.

scenes.tts: Third, the sensor, which measures the variable. Temperature-sensitive nerve cells in the skin and brain do this. Fourth, the integrator, a region of the brain called the hypothalamus. It compares the sensed value with the set point and sends out a command.
scenes.visual: Box 3 lights: 'sensor', with a cartoon of nerve endings in a skin strip and a small brain icon, sending a pulse along a line. Box 4 lights: 'integrator (hypothalamus)', a small brain region highlighted; an on-screen comparison 'sensed vs set point' with a '>' sign; an arrow labelled 'command' leaves it.
scenes.narration: Third, the sensor, which measures the variable. Temperature-sensitive nerve cells in the skin and brain do this. Fourth, the integrator, a region of the brain called the hypothalamus. It compares the sensed value with the set point and sends out a command.

scenes.tts: Fifth, the effectors, which change the variable. As he warms, skin blood vessels widen and carry heat to the surface. Sweat glands release sweat, which removes heat as it evaporates.
scenes.visual: Box 5 lights: 'effector'. The command arrow reaches a skin cartoon: a blood vessel widens (label 'skin vessels widen'), and droplets bead from a sweat gland (label 'sweat glands') and drift off as wisps (label 'evaporation removes heat'). The loop closes back to the TEAL bar, which stays near the dashed line.
scenes.narration: Fifth, the effectors, which change the variable. As he warms, skin blood vessels widen and carry heat to the surface. Sweat glands release sweat, which removes heat as it evaporates.

scenes.tts: Cool him instead, and other effectors take over. Skin vessels narrow to keep heat in, and muscles shiver. Either way, the push points back toward the set point. That is negative feedback.
scenes.visual: The ORANGE outside bar drops below the dashed line; the ORANGE leak arrow flips to point out of the body. The TEAL bar dips slightly. The effector box swaps icons: a narrowing vessel ('skin vessels narrow') and a shaking arm ('shivering'). The TEAL push-back arrow flips to point UP toward the dashed line. Caption fades in: 'negative feedback = push-back toward the set point, from either side'.
scenes.narration: Cool him instead, and other effectors take over. Skin vessels narrow to keep heat in, and muscles shiver. Either way, the push points back toward the set point. That is negative feedback.

scenes.tts: So how far does the inside follow the outside? That depends on how strong push-back is compared with leak. Strength means the pull for each degree of gap.
scenes.visual: Clear to a clean schematic: ORANGE outside bar on the left, TEAL inside bar on the right with its dashed TEAL set point, ORANGE leak arrow and TEAL push-back arrow between them. Below, two round dials: an ORANGE dial labelled 'leak strength' and a TEAL dial labelled 'push-back strength', both needles at mid. A small caption under the dials: 'strength = pull per degree of gap'. Label 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: So how far does the inside follow the outside? That depends on how strong push-back is compared with leak. Strength means the pull for each degree of gap.

scenes.tts: Set the two dials equal, so push-back is exactly as strong as leak. Then raise the outside by ten degrees. Does the inside follow all of it, half, or none?
scenes.visual: The TEAL dial turns until it matches the ORANGE dial; on screen 'push-back strength = leak strength'. The ORANGE outside bar rises; a bracket labels the rise '+10'. Three option cards appear above the TEAL bar: 'all', 'half', 'none'.
scenes.narration: Set the two dials equal, so push-back is exactly as strong as leak. Then raise the outside by ten degrees. Does the inside follow all of it, half, or none?

scenes.visual: Hold. The three option cards pulse gently. A small countdown ring fills.

scenes.tts: Half. In this simple model, the two pulls always balance once the inside settles. With equal strengths, they balance when the two gaps are equal, halfway.
scenes.visual: The 'half' card lights. The TEAL inside bar rises and settles; a bracket labels its rise '+5', and two equal brackets show the gap to the outside (5) and the gap from the set point (5). As it settles, the ORANGE leak arrow thins and the TEAL push-back arrow thickens until the two are equally thick; tag 'settled: the two pulls are equal'. On screen, the computed rule fades in: 'inside shift = outside shift × leak strength ÷ (leak strength + push-back strength)' and below it '10 × 1 ÷ (1 + 1) = 5'. A small grey tag under the rule: 'simple model: after settling, set point fixed, effectors below their limit'.
scenes.narration: Half. In this simple model, the two pulls always balance once the inside settles. With equal strengths, they balance when the two gaps are equal, halfway.

scenes.tts: Turn push-back strength down to zero, and the inside follows the outside completely, like the egg. That end of the dial is a conformer. Turn push-back strength far above leak strength, and the inside barely moves. That end is a regulator.
scenes.visual: The TEAL push-back strength dial sweeps to zero: the TEAL push-back arrow vanishes, and as the ORANGE bar swings up and down the TEAL bar tracks it exactly; label 'conformer: fraction near 1'. The TEAL dial sweeps to max: the TEAL bar barely moves as the ORANGE bar swings, and whenever it settles the two arrows are equally thick; label 'regulator: fraction near 0'. A small computed curve of fraction against push-back strength ÷ leak strength draws beneath the dials, falling from 1 toward 0.
scenes.narration: Turn push-back strength down to zero, and the inside follows the outside completely, like the egg. That end of the dial is a conformer. Turn push-back strength far above leak strength, and the inside barely moves. That end is a regulator.

scenes.tts: Back to the hot room. Blagden's body pushed back, so his temperature barely moved. The trials lasted minutes, so they show push-back, not its strength. The egg had no push-back at all.
scenes.visual: Return to the stove room. Blagden sits with a TEAL push-back arrow and an ORANGE leak arrow, neither drawn to a measured size; his TEAL bar holds by the dashed line. The egg beside him has only the ORANGE leak arrow and its TEAL bar climbing toward the air's level. Small tag 'brief trials, minutes long'. Label 'schematic'.
scenes.narration: Back to the hot room. Blagden's body pushed back, so his temperature barely moved. The trials lasted minutes, so they show push-back, not its strength. The egg had no push-back at all.

scenes.visual: End card with Hex, the hexagon mascot, beside the line: 'The stronger the push-back compared with leak, the less the inside follows.' ORANGE leak-strength dial and TEAL push-back-strength dial frame the line.
